correctness.rationale: The exact normalized one-trial probability uses the free lattice Bessel amplitude. The geometric renewal expectation is 1/(r q), despite within-trial dependence. The Laplace transform gives the stated real Legendre Q. A positive toroidal integral proves the local uniform Q-to-K0 limit; its global bound Q<=K0(n eta), with split at a=1, prevents every maximizing sequence from escaping 0 or infinity. Strict growth of alpha K1/K0 proves uniqueness of the limiting maximizer and both global optimization limits, not just numerical convergence. Independently implemented quadrature, finite matrix propagators and optimized finite n check the normalizations (VERIFY_OK 15+8+16+5+4). Residual proof assumptions are explicitly bounded self-adjoint homogeneous hopping, n>=1 and positive rates; no finite-test-to-infinite inference.

originality.rationale: The assessed statement is the complete globally optimized large-distance exponential one-shot interrogation theorem, not the known Bessel-Laplace identity or renewal recipe. Source-specific full-text comparisons show that Poisson continuation after null measurement, fixed-period restart, uniformly jittered periodic measurement and fully reset independent exponential trials are distinguishable stochastic/quantum protocols. Targeted searches of primary literature and mathematical records found no directly matching theorem or dominating stronger claim. Residual risk is unlocated broader general restart literature; independent priority audit has not occurred.
residual_risks: An unidentified abstract renewal or classical waiting-time optimization theorem might imply the K0 rate law after specialization; no exhaustive priority certification.
The protocol is idealized and not optimal across different waiting-time distributions, multimeasurement restart schedules or nonzero control/readout costs.

The theorem gives a nontrivial sharp optimized n^2 law and universal transcendentally specified optimal measurement clock, contrasting ballistic propagation with actual search performance. This is a structural quantitative benchmark at every far-target distance, not a renamed known table entry or an arbitrary special finite case; no claim of advantage over all protocols.
